The material states that this area is located near Lake Huron, Lake Erie, and the Ottawa River, and has hilly land, gravelly-soil plains, and sandy and clayey soil plains, and is one of Canada’s agricultural regions. Reasoning: this place has lakes, rivers, and certain soil conditions, so water sources and soil are not the greatest limitations; but it is still located in southern Canada at a relatively high latitude, and crop farming requires sufficient accumulated temperature and a relatively long growing season, while high-latitude regions have cold winters and a relatively short frost-free period. Therefore, the greatest obstacle to the development of crop farming should be insufficient heat conditions.
